title: Procedural Spider Locomotion on Terrain
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a procedural spider locomotion system walking on a terrain surface using Three.js (via CDN). Load the asset 'ABeautifulGame.glb' using GLTFLoader as a decorative chess-set landmark placed at the terrain center.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 12, 20) looking at origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Add a hemisphere light (sky: 0x88aacc, ground: 0x443322, intensity 1.0) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with shadows enabled.
- Renderer with shadow mapping enabled, antialias, size fills viewport.
- Sky-blue background (0x7ec8e3).

## Terrain
- Generate a PlaneGeometry(40, 40, 80, 80) rotated to be horizontal (XZ plane).
- Displace vertices using simplex-style noise: y = 1.5 * sin(x*0.3) * cos(z*0.3) + 0.5 * sin(x*0.7+1) * cos(z*0.5+2). Recompute normals.
- Use MeshStandardMaterial with color 0x5a8f3c (grass green).
- Implement a function getTerrainHeight(x, z) that returns the interpolated y-height at any (x,z) coordinate using the same formula.

## GLB Asset
- Load 'ABeautifulGame.glb' and place it at position (0, getTerrainHeight(0,0), 0). Scale it to (0.5, 0.5, 0.5). It serves as a landmark the spider can walk around.

## Procedural Spider
- Build a spider body from a sphere (radius 0.5) colored 0x222222 and a smaller head sphere (radius 0.3) offset forward.
- The spider has 8 legs, 4 on each side, arranged symmetrically. Each leg has 3 segments (upper: length 1.0, middle: length 1.2, lower: length 1.0) built from CylinderGeometry(0.05, 0.04, segLength). Joints connect segments.
- Each leg has a 'foot' target position on the terrain and a current interpolated position. The foot tip (end effector) should be solved via a simple 2-joint IK (or iterative FABRIK) to reach the target.
- Leg attachment points on the body: distribute 4 per side at angles [-40, -15, 15, 40] degrees from the forward axis, offset 0.4 from body center laterally.

## Locomotion System
- The spider moves with WASD keys: W=forward, S=backward, A=rotate left, D=rotate right. Movement speed: 3.0 units/sec. Rotation speed: 2.0 rad/sec.
- The spider body follows the terrain height with smooth interpolation (lerp factor 0.1 per frame toward getTerrainHeight at body XZ).
- Implement a gait system: legs step in an alternating tetrapod gait pattern. Group legs into two sets of 4 (legs 0,3,5,6 and legs 1,2,4,7). When one group is planted, the other can step.
- A leg initiates a step when its foot target is more than 1.5 units from its ideal resting position (relative to body). During a step, the foot lifts in an arc (0.5 units above terrain) and moves to the new target over 0.2 seconds.
- The ideal resting position for each leg is computed relative to the spider's current position and orientation, projected onto the terrain.

## Controls & UI
- Add a DOM panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text, id='hud-panel') showing:
  - Spider position (x, z) rounded to 2 decimals
  - Current speed
  - Number of legs currently stepping
  - Gait group indicator (A or B)
  - Total steps taken counter
- Add a button id='btn-toggle-gait' that toggles between 'tetrapod' and 'wave' gait. Wave gait steps legs sequentially (one at a time, indices 0-7 in order).
- Add a button id='btn-reset' that resets the spider to position (5, terrainY, 5) facing +Z, resets step counter to 0.
- Add a button id='btn-speed-up' that increases movement speed by 1.0 (max 8.0).
- Add a button id='btn-speed-down' that decreases movement speed by 1.0 (min 1.0).
- Add a checkbox id='chk-debug' that toggles visibility of debug spheres (small red spheres at each foot target, small blue spheres at each foot current position).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
- spiderPosition: {x, y, z} — body world position
- spiderRotation: number — Y-axis rotation in radians
- spiderSpeed: number — current movement speed setting
- isMoving: boolean — true if any movement key is held
- legStates: array of 8 objects each with {isSteppig: bool, footPosition: {x,y,z}, targetPosition: {x,y,z}, distanceToTarget: number}
- legsCurrentlyStepping: number — count of legs mid-step
- gaitMode: 'tetrapod' | 'wave'
- gaitGroup: 'A' | 'B' | index (for wave)
- totalStepsTaken: number
- terrainHeightAtSpider: number — getTerrainHeight at spider XZ
- bodyTerrainDelta: number — abs(spiderPosition.y - terrainHeightAtSpider)
- glbLoaded: boolean
- glbPosition: {x, y, z}
- debugVisible: boolean
- frameCount: number — incremented each frame
- legPositionsValid: boolean — true if no leg foot position contains NaN
- ikConverged: boolean — true if all legs' end effectors are within 0.3 of their targets when planted
- speedClamped: boolean — true if speed is within [1.0, 8.0]
physics_constraints: Spider body Y must track terrain height within 0.5 units tolerance. All leg foot positions must be NaN-free at all times. Leg step arcs must not penetrate terrain (foot Y >= terrainHeight - 0.1 during step). Speed must be clamped to [1.0, 8.0]. In tetrapod gait, at most 4 legs step simultaneously. In wave gait, at most 1 leg steps at a time. IK end effectors must converge within 0.3 units of target when leg is planted.
